translation_notes: Three triple patterns around fixed IRIs and one projected variable, results read only as `value[0]`: a basic graph pattern whose result shape nothing needs, so m{ }(runner.app.db) instead of s{ SELECT ... }. The comprehension `[value[0] for value in values]` becomes `[value for value in m{ ... }(db)]` (m{ } yields the bare term for one variable): hence minor-restructuring. `a` stands for rdf:type; <bnode:...> is an ordinary IRI with the bnode: scheme in the source.

The source decorates the test with @disable_test, which replaces it by a function that only prints: as the source applies it, the SPARQL is dead code. Context shim ingest_shim.py keeps disable_test line for line and adds a switch EXERCISE_BODY; the driver sets it so that both sides run the body (otherwise the check would compare two prints). `Runner` is a unittest.TestCase stand-in for the nanomine runner (app.db a Graph, expected_data a dict).

A bug of the source is kept: with expected_value=None the code assigns expected_authors, so assertCountEqual receives None and raises TypeError; the driver exercises it (and the KeyError when expected_data lacks the key). Thirteen calls: pass, order, wrong values, fewer values, duplicate triple, missing type, missing link, other sample. Deleting the type pattern of the translation fails the check (verified).
